title: Guide: the clique lesson as a rule
description: The refinement "delete one of the clique's nodes" written as rules of a program part refine(i), grounded for every counterexample. See the guide page "Refinements that are rules".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% The Paley graph on n nodes (n a prime of the form 4m + 1): two nodes are joined when
% their difference is a square modulo n.
node(0..n-1).
square((X*X) \ n) :- X = 1..n-1.
edge(U,V) :- node(U), node(V), U < V, square((V-U) \ n).
fragments.description: The Paley graph on n nodes. Added to every solver.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most k nodes to delete.
{ del(V) : node(V) } k.
#show del/1.
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): at most k deleted nodes.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The check sees which nodes are deleted.
glue(del(V)) :- node(V).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the deleted nodes.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: c nodes that are not deleted and pairwise joined.
c { q(V) : node(V) } c.
:- q(V), del(V).
:- q(U), q(V), U < V, not edge(U,V).
#show q/1.

% No relevant/1 rules: the loop passes the clique q/1 to the refine part.
fragments.description: Looks for a clique of c nodes that survives the deletions (solver C).

fragments.name: refine
fragments.text:
#program refine(i).
% cex(i,q(V)): node V is in the i-th surviving clique. One of its nodes must go.
hit(i) :- cex(i,q(V)), del(V).
:- not hit(i).
fragments.description: Rules grounded once per counterexample (#program refine(i)).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction + refine
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(q/1))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))
